dimensions.reason: Procedure: Academic Integrity (N027, 5.4 and 5.6) assigns investigation and decision authority to the Course Coordinator, Academic Integrity Officer, Head of School/Director, and Discipline Committees, explicitly linked to Policy: Student Appeals (N034, 23-24).

documents_checked.text:
5.4 Contract cheating
5.4.1 All breaches of academic integrity involving contract cheating are considered to be
student misconduct.
5.4.2 If the suspected breach of academic integrity involves an allegation of contract
cheating, the course coordinator will refer it to the Academic Integrity Officer for
investigation to decide if it can be substantiated.
5.4.3 If the Academic Integrity Officer decides it is likely that contract cheating has occurred,
they will notify the course coordinator who will report the matter to the appropriate
head of school or director. (refer to clause 5.2.2 of this procedure)
5.4.3.1 If the incident of contract cheating involves multiple students, the Academic
Integrity Officer will also notify the Pro Vice Chancellor, Education and the
Deputy Vice-Chancellor, Academic.
5.4.4 If the Academic Integrity Officer decides that contract cheating cannot be
substantiated, they will notify the course coordinator and provide the reason for their
decision.

4.4.1 A level three breach of academic integrity may involve any of the following:
4.4.1.1 any form of cheating, including contract cheating
4.4.1.2 fabrication or falsification of data or other information, or

lacks integrity; but which
4.4.1.4 is unlikely to have included committing an offence that might lead to legal
proceedings.

review_route_evidence.text:

24.1 A Student may appeal the decision of the University Discipline Committee to the Student
Misconduct Appeals Committee in accordance with the General Regulations
24.2 Grounds for appeal: The Student may only appeal on the following grounds:
24.2.1 the University Discipline Committee failed to comply with Procedural Fairness;
24.2.2 the Student has evidence relating to the allegation that was not reasonably available at
the time of the University Discipline Committee hearing and that, if available, may have
reasonably affected the decision of the University Discipline Committee or the penalty

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Prevention or enforceable refusal of unverified AI-produced assessment being claimed as the student's own.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: Policy: Academic Integrity (N028, 4.5.2.3-4.5.2.4) and Procedure: Academic Integrity (N027, 4.4.1.1, 5.4) prohibit and enforce against unverified AI-produced assessment submissions as unauthorised Gen-AI and contract cheating.
case_summary.case_note: Notre Dame explicitly prohibits submitting unverified AI-generated work under Policy: Academic Integrity (N028, 4.5.2.3-4.5.2.4), classifying it as unauthorised Gen-AI use or contract cheating. Procedure: Academic Integrity (N027) and Policy: Student Appeals (N034) provide a complete investigation, penalty, and appeal pathway; Protocol v1.1 critical-risk criteria were adopted after preliminary review.
